title: One pie, more and more visitors
_map: Sharing pies (Y1–2). Big idea: quarters and thirds are equal parts; 3/4 is 3 of 4 parts. Creative: cut pies fairly for 3 or 4 villagers; what if a new visitor arrives?
_story: Steve baked a pie for the farm animals. 2 friends, then 4, then 3 arrive. Ismaeel cuts it into equal parts each time, names quarters and thirds, then a surprise visitor arrives.
_stepChain: halves (halves) → 4 friends: 4 equal parts → quarter → 3 friends: thirds → the fraction number: bottom is how many parts, top is how many we have → 3 of 4 is three quarters → more friends, smaller slices

talk.ask: Would you rather have a third of a pie or a quarter? Why?
talk.goodAnswer: a third: sharing between fewer people makes bigger slices.
the pie is cut into 4 equal parts, and you have 3 of them.

handsOn: Cut a sandwich, a pizza or a pancake into halves, then quarters. Then try thirds (it's harder!). Which slices are biggest?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Mmm! I baked an apple pie! Two friends came round, so I cut it in half. One half each!
Knock knock! Two more friends! Now there are 4. So we cut the pie into 4 equal parts. Each part is called a quarter.
Now you cut! Pick how many friends are sharing, then tap the hammer. Watch the slices. What happens to their size?
With 3 friends, the pie is cut into 3 equal parts. Each part is called a third. More friends means smaller slices!

Here's how we write a slice of pie, with one number on top of another. The bottom number says how many equal parts the pie is cut into: 4. The top number says how many parts we have: 3. Three quarters!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: The pie is cut into thirds, for 3 friends. But surprise! Knock knock! A fourth friend! I'll keep the same 3 slices and squeeze up!

question.prompt: What's the fair thing to do?
question.onRight: Yes! 4 friends need 4 equal slices. Cut it into quarters!

0.mistake: thinks squeezing makes room for more people without re-cutting
0.hint: Count the friends and the slices. Does everyone get one?
0.say: 4 friends, but only 3 slices? Someone gets nothing! To be fair, cut the pie into 4 equal parts: quarters.

question.reveal: 4 friends, 4 equal slices. A quarter each!

rule.ask: What's a quarter? What does three quarters mean? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: A quarter is one of four equal parts. Three quarters means three of those parts. More people sharing means smaller slices.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! Which is bigger: one half of a pie, or two quarters of the same pie?
bonus.reveal: They're the same! Two quarters fit exactly into one half. You'll explore that next!
